chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Harun ibn Harijah who said:

Indeed Abu Murad sent a camel and ordered the one he sent with it to clip its hair and shave it on such and such a day. I said to him, 'It is not appropriate for you to wear clothes.' So he sent me to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was in Al-Hirah. I said to him, 'Abu Murad did such and such, and he cannot leave the clothes because of the place of Abu Ja'far.' He said, 'Order him to wear the clothes and slaughter a cow on the day of sacrifice as expiation for wearing the clothes.'
The Shaykh (peace be upon him) said: And it is disliked to pray on the road to Mecca in three places.

key_terms.الثِّيَاب: Clothes (specifically non-silk garments forbidden for men in Ihram)
key_terms.يُقَلِّدَ: To clip the hair (of the animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for an Imam who wears clothes while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *rukhsah* (dispensation) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribed slaughtering a cow as expiation for wearing non-silk garments during Ihram due to social necessity (*mugharadah*) rather than mere negligence. The ruling highlights the distinction between intentional violation and unavoidable circumstance, while the appended note by Shaykh al-Tusi regarding disliked prayer locations on the road to Mecca reflects the practical application of ritual purity and respect for the sacred path.
